record.original_question: For random n x n band matrices H with bandwidth w <= n and independent entries H_ij inside the band, can one prove the Fyodorov-Mirlin conjecture that the local eigenvalue statistics are in the GUE universality class when w is much larger than sqrt(n), but become Poisson when w is much smaller than sqrt(n), in both the real symmetric and complex Hermitian settings?

evidence.quote: An open problem of great, ongoing interest is the question of the behavior of random n x n band matrices H with bandwidth w <= n, H_ij = 0 if |i - j| >= w. The long-standing conjecture of V. Fyodorov and A. Mirlin [59] from 1991 is that for iid H_ij, |i - j| < w, with w >> sqrt(n), the local statistics of the eigenvalues of H are GUE, but for w << sqrt(n), the behavior is Poisson.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $w = w(n) \le n$ be a bandwidth parameter, and consider the ensemble of random $n \times n$ band matrices $H = (H_{ij})$ defined as follows. The entries satisfy $H_{ij} = 0$ whenever $|i-j| \ge w$, and the entries $\{H_{ij} : |i-j| < w,\ i \le j\}$ are independent random variables (with $H_{ji}$ determined by the symmetry/Hermitian constraint). Two settings are considered:

(a) Real symmetric: $H_{ij} = H_{ji} \in \mathbb{R}$, i.i.d. (up to symmetry) with mean zero and finite variance.

(b) Complex Hermitian: $H_{ij} = \overline{H_{ji}} \in \mathbb{C}$, with independent real and imaginary parts (mean zero, finite variance), again i.i.d. inside the band.

After rescaling so that the empirical spectral measure converges to the semicircle law, consider the local eigenvalue statistics of $H$ in the bulk of the spectrum (e.g., the local correlation functions on scale $1/n$, or the gap distribution).

Prove the following Fyodorov–Mirlin transition in both settings (a) and (b):

(i) If $w \gg \sqrt{n}$ (i.e., $w/\sqrt{n} \to \infty$), then the local eigenvalue statistics of $H$ converge to those of the corresponding Gaussian invariant ensemble (GOE in case (a), GUE in case (b)).

(ii) If $w \ll \sqrt{n}$ (i.e., $w/\sqrt{n} \to 0$ with $w \to \infty$), then the local eigenvalue statistics converge to those of a Poisson point process (with intensity given by the semicircle density).
artifact.status_search_result: The Fyodorov–Mirlin √n conjecture (1991) for one-dimensional random band matrices remains open in general. Substantial partial progress has been made on the GUE/delocalized side: GUE-type local statistics and quantum unique ergodicity of eigenvectors have been established for bandwidths well above √n in Hermitian Gaussian-like models (work of Bourgade, Yau, Yin, and collaborators), and rigorous results have been obtained in special Gaussian or chiral models. The Poisson side for w ≪ √n is essentially still open, and the full conjecture covering both regimes in real symmetric and complex Hermitian band matrices has not been proved.

status_evidence.title: Random band matrices (P. Bourgade, ICM Proceedings)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys the Fyodorov–Mirlin transition conjecture at threshold w ~ √n and partial results toward GUE universality for w ≫ √n.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is described as a major open problem with partial progress on the delocalized side.

status_evidence.title: Chiral random band matrices at zero energy
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the Fyodorov–Mirlin √N transition rigorously in a special chiral band matrix model at zero energy.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous proof of the conjecture is available only in special models, not in the general band matrix ensemble.
